assets.prompt:
Create ONE original isolated city miniature asset for a historical hex strategy game. This is a single complete directly generated sprite, not a sheet, collage, panel, screenshot or landscape. Premium restrained hand-painted 2.5D miniature realism, matching a muted olive-green strategic map with blue-green water. Elevated fixed orthographic camera 50 degrees above ground, north at the top, upper-left daylight, clear cool lower-right wall shadows. Coherent large gray-slate tiled roof planes, warm pale-gray brick walls, substantial architectural volume. Design the silhouette and roof groups to remain legible when the entire urban cluster is displayed only 90-110 pixels wide. Use crisp readable shapes and deliberate value separation, no photographic micro-noise or blurry miniature effect. Compact connected urban mass filling 78 percent of the canvas width, generous transparent margin all around. Broadest urban silhouette at the lower middle, complete building edges visible. Fully zero-alpha transparent exterior including corners; a short soft contact shadow only beneath the buildings. Do not paint a ground island, grass halo, paved square pedestal or rectangular base. No people, soldiers, military flag, coats of arms, text, UI, labels, hexagons, writing, frames, watermark, modern automobile, power pole, skyscraper or modern infrastructure. No detached objects or extra samples. This is an unnamed representative pre-1940 architectural SYMBOL, not a purported surveyed plan of a named city. Avoid palaces, pagodas, monuments, religious icons and invented famous landmarks. No rivers, coastlines, boats, fields or rail tracks: geographic geometry and facilities are separate game layers. Do not reproduce any existing commercial game artwork.
Regional architecture: traditional north Chinese gray-brick courtyard street blocks. Depict an URBAN CITY, clearly denser and larger than a county courtyard: 18-24 tightly grouped low houses and shops arranged in three irregular connected roof masses, two narrow readable alleys, a few enclosed small courts. Broad long muted charcoal-gray ridgelines, varied roof heights, mostly one or two stories. A low front gateway to one internal lane, without a surrounding city wall or grand tower. Roof groups should create an asymmetrical compact silhouette with three deep shadow cuts and a restrained light wall edge toward the front. Very little vegetation. Keep the large roof planes and readable front wall rhythm; do not substitute two grand symmetrical courtyards or a single temple compound.
